title: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines
abstract: arXiv:2611.25955v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI platforms are becoming a major gateway to news and current events. This shift risks amplifying existing geographical biases that favour narratives from wealthier countries over those from the Global South. This is particularly relevant in Latin America, which accounts for the largest share of AI usage in the Global South. We examine how information about Latin America changes when users shift from conventional search engines to LLM-based search. We construct a dataset of 1,901 current events across nine Latin American countries, craft realistic queries, and submit them to three search engines and four language models. We vary query language and user location to represent local, diaspora, tourist, and foreign user scenarios. Across 49,207 requests and 8,834 unique domains, language models return a less diverse set of news sources than search engines. translated_title: 拉丁美洲的网络搜索：语言模型使用的新闻来源比搜索引擎更少本地化且多样性更低
translated_abstract: AI平台正在成为人们获取新闻和时事的主要入口。这一转变可能会加剧现有的地理偏见，即偏向来自较富裕国家的叙述而忽视全球南方国家的声音。这对拉丁美洲尤为相关，因为该地区在全球南方的AI使用量中占比最大。我们研究了当用户从传统搜索引擎转向基于大语言模型的搜索时，关于拉丁美洲的信息会发生怎样的变化。我们构建了一个涵盖九个拉丁美洲国家、包含1,901个时事事件的数据集，设计了贴近现实的查询，并将其提交给三个搜索引擎和四个语言模型。我们改变了查询语言和用户所在位置，以代表本地用户、海外侨民、游客和外国用户四种场景。在49,207次请求和8,834个独立域名中，语言模型返回的新闻来源多样性低于搜索引擎。在不同用户类型下，语言模型返回的国内新闻占比表现不一致……
tldr: 本研究通过对拉丁美洲九国时事的大规模查询实验发现，基于语言模型的搜索返回的新闻来源多样性低于传统搜索引擎，且本地新闻占比因用户类型而表现不一致，揭示了AI搜索可能加剧地理偏见的风险。
en_tdlr: Large-scale experiments across nine Latin American countries show that LLM-based search returns a less diverse set of news sources than traditional search engines, with inconsistent shares of domestic news across user types, revealing how AI search may amplify geographical bias.
